analysis.title: Historic Degrossing: Hedge Funds Dump Most Tech Stock Since Sept 2024
key_insights: Goldman's HF VIP longs vs. most-shorted names basket (GSTHVIPP) finished down about 4.2% through early afternoon Thursday, its worst one-day move since 2011, and is down 10.4% month to date.
The only larger one-day drop on Bloomberg's chart was -8.26% on August 8, 2011, the first trading day after S&P downgraded the US.

As of Thursday midday, Goldman Prime Brokerage had Fundamental L/S funds down 1.1%, Systematic funds down 1.2% and Multi-Strats down 1.4%. This was the first time since Covid that all three strategies fell more than 1% on the same day.
Hedge funds de-grossed global equities in 7 of the past 8 sessions, and the pace has been accelerating. The last such streak was April 2026, and none occurred in 2025.
October 22 was the 5th largest de-grossing event of the year at -1.6 sigma. It was driven entirely by long selling and was the largest long selling since September 2025.

Nearly all major regions saw risk unwinds, led by North America (long sales), Europe (long sales exceeded short covers) and EM Asia (long sales exceeded short sales). China and Hong Kong were the most net sold in Asia, while selling in Taiwan, Korea and Japan was more moderate.
9 of 11 global sectors were de-grossed, led by Info Tech and Industrials.

Info Tech saw long selling alongside short additions. It was the largest net selling since September 2024, every industry was net sold, and Semi & Semi Equipment was the most de-grossed. Fundamental L/S funds did most of it, with multi-strats and quants also selling.
Semi & Semi Equipment allocations have dropped to levels seen earlier in the year.
Industrials was de-grossed mainly by multi-strats and quants, with every industry de-grossed. It was the third largest de-grossing day of the year.
Goldman's global AI basket (GSXGGLAI) saw the largest net selling since end of July, and net/gross allocations have fallen back to the lows seen after the July moves.
Prime book gross leverage fell 0.4 pts to 312.3% (79th percentile 1-year, 96th percentile 5-year). Net leverage fell 2.1 pts to 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year, 37th percentile 5-year).
Global Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 0.4 pts to 211.7% (63rd percentile 1-year, 92nd percentile 5-year). Net leverage fell 3.1 pts to 47% (1st percentile 3-year, 5th percentile 5-year).

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds made their largest net sales of the sector since September 2024, with every industry net sold and semis the most de-grossed.
Multi-strats and quants de-grossed every industry, making it the third largest de-grossing day of the year.

risk_factors: Continued de-grossing by hedge funds, with the pace accelerating.
Crowded long positions in tech and semis are being liquidated, and the long-vs-short basket is falling sharply.
Gross leverage remains high on a 5-year view (96th percentile) even after the unwind, which leaves room for further selling.
